root_cause.text: The `hwdep_read` function in the ALSA firewire-motu driver fails to verify if the remaining user buffer space is large enough to accommodate a 4-byte DSP event before writing it using `put_user()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff in `sound/firewire/motu/motu-hwdep.c` adds the check `consumed + sizeof(ev) > count` before calling `put_user(ev, ptr)` to prevent writing beyond the user buffer boundary when `count` is not aligned to 4 bytes.

intent_record.how: It prevents writing data past the end of the user-provided buffer, returning an error if the remaining space is insufficient.

candidates.rationale: The loop condition only checks if 'consumed < count', which allows the loop to proceed even if there is only 1 byte left in the user buffer. Since 'ev' is a 4-byte DSP event, writing it with 'put_user' will cause an out-of-bounds write.
This is part of the loop condition that fails to verify if there is enough space (at least 4 bytes) left in the user buffer before copying the event.

vuln_statements.explanation: The loop condition only checks if 'consumed < count', which allows the loop to proceed even if there is less than 4 bytes (the size of the DSP event) left in the user buffer. This leads to an out-of-bounds write when writing the 4-byte event to the user buffer.

This is the second part of the loop condition that retrieves the event to be copied, but fails to ensure that the remaining buffer size is sufficient (at least 4 bytes) before proceeding with the copy operation.

    ALSA: firewire-motu: notify event for parameter change in register DSP model
    
    This commit copies queued event for change of register DSP into
    userspace when application operates ALSA hwdep character device.
    The notification occurs only when packet streaming is running.
    
    Signed-off-by: Takashi Sakamoto <o-takashi@sakamocchi.jp>
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerable code in `hwdep_read`. Specifically, the loop condition `while (consumed < count && ...)` only checks if `consumed` is strictly less than `count` (i.e., at least 1 byte is remaining). However, inside the loop, `put_user(ev, ptr)` writes a 4-byte `u32` value to the user buffer. If the remaining space (`count - consumed`) is less than 4 bytes (e.g., 1, 2, or 3 bytes), `put_user` will write past the user-specified buffer boundary `count`, leading to an out-of-bounds write.
